title: SLO decision framework for priority fences and fallback scheduler
creator: Ava Chen
description: Define a readable, implementable SLO/SLI declaration and enforcement model that supports per-endpoint and per-model fidelity contracts, priority fencing for high-value customers, and a dynamic fallback scheduler that activates model-variant or regional fallback and soft-eviction load-shedding when error budgets approach exhaustion.
background: We routinely see transient bursts where lower-priority traffic causes elevated latency and quality regressions for premium routes. Current SLO artifacts are heterogeneous across teams and do not encode priority fences or automated fallback actions. This ticket scopes a canonical SLO/SLI declaration schema plus the decision rules for automated fallback and eviction so we can enforce predictable behavior across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
proposed_solution: 1) Define a compact SLI schema (latency quantiles, success-rate by response-quality test, model-quality score) that can be attached to endpoints and model variants. 2) Define priority fences (gold, standard, best-effort) that map to traffic-currency and preemption rules. 3) Implement a policy engine that consumes SLI telemetry + error budget burn-rate to drive a fallback scheduler: soft eviction -> model-variant fallback -> regional failover -> circuit breaker. 4) Expose enforcement knobs in Console and a canary circuit in runtime for gradual rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical SLI schema documented in Confluence with examples for chat/generate/embedding routes
Policy engine PoC runs in staging and triggers simulated fallback actions when synthetic error budgets are burned
Console UI shows per-endpoint priority fence and current error budget utilization with drilldowns
Automated tests for hysteresis (no flip-flop) and priority-preempt behavior included in CI
Runbook updated with clear operator play for manual override and rollback
monitoring_and_telemetry: New dashboards: per-endpoint SLI heatmap, error-budget burn-rate per priority band, active-fallback-actions timeline
Alerting: burn-rate > 2x baseline for 5m (P1 pager for reliability on gold routes), burn-rate > 3x triggers automated soft-eviction
Logs: policy decisions recorded with decision-reason, affected-tenant, pre/post-metrics
Tracing: sampled traces for requests affected by fallback to validate quality delta
rollout_plan: Week 1: finalize schema and policy decision matrix; internal review with PM/Runtime/Console
Week 2: implement policy engine PoC + simulator that replays historical incidents to validate thresholds
Week 3: deploy to staging with canary for 10% of traffic on non-production orgs
Week 4: expand to internal production tenants (non-customer) and validate observability
Week 5: gradual rollout to customers with release notes and opt-in flag, monitor for 2 weeks before enabling by default
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Aggressive soft-eviction may harm quality for bursts that self-resolve. Mitigation: enforce hysteresis windows and minimum hold-time for eviction decisions.
Risk: Incorrect SLI mapping for multimodal endpoints. Mitigation: provide per-route example templates and require model owners to verify with smoke tests.
Risk: Priority fencing could starve best-effort workloads. Mitigation: reserve a minimal capacity floor for best-effort and expose quotas in Console.
Risk: Operator confusion during rollout. Mitigation: clear runbook, UI visibility, and an emergency disable switch for the policy engine.
open_questions: Should the SLI quality metric be model-dependent (e.g., embedding cosine threshold) or unified across product surfaces?
What's the default reserved capacity for best-effort traffic in Dedicated pools? Should it be percent-based or absolute?
How should we price or expose preemption to Dedicated customers — as an explicit feature or implicit behavior?
Do we need an audit trail for every fallback decision for compliance in Private deployments?
decisions: Decision: Use p95 and p99 latency plus a response-quality SLI (binary pass/fail against a promptset) as the canonical SLI bundle for conversational routes.
Decision: Priority fences will be Gold/Standard/BestEffort mapped to preemption weight 100/60/10 and a minimum capacity reservation for BestEffort at 5%.
Decision: Fallback scheduler order: soft-eviction -> model-variant fallback -> regional shift -> hard circuit-breaker. Hysteresis of 120s between state transitions.
Decision: Policy engine will be opt-in per-organization initially and default-on for internal system tenants.
implementation_notes: Policy engine will subscribe to aggregated burn-rate metrics exported from the SLI aggregator service (sli-agg).
We'll implement an action-orchestrator in runtime that can apply model-variant switches or return 503 with retry-after headers for hard circuit breaks.
KV cache thresholds should be considered as a multiplier for effective capacity (i.e., high cache hit reduces invocation cost and should bias decisions away from eviction).
Add feature flag hooks for per-tenant opt-in and a global emergency-disable in Console.
